name: Recovery of Encrypted Personal Drive — Active Crime Scene, the Gray Zone 8
posted_by: Dela Okonkwo (private individual, the Gray Zone 8, vouched by one C-tier broker)
target: One personal encrypted storage drive, matte black, approximately 6cm, standard hardened casing — last known location: apartment 14C, Kessler Block, the Gray Zone 8, currently an active Arcturus Civil Security forensic hold
objective: Enter apartment 14C in Kessler Block before Arcturus completes its forensic sweep — estimated 48-hour window — and recover the encrypted drive from its hiding location (behind the ventilation panel in the kitchen, third grille from the left). Return the drive only to Dela Okonkwo in person.
location: Kessler Block, apartment 14C, the Gray Zone 8, GLMZ South Corridor
payout: Φ8,000 — all of Dela Okonkwo's available liquid funds
deadline: 48 hours before Arcturus forensic sweep concludes and the apartment is cleared for evidence retention
complications: Arcturus has posted a forensic hold notice on the apartment; entry during a forensic hold is a chargeable offense that Arcturus Civil Security takes seriously because it sets precedent — contractors caught inside face processing, not just removal
The apartment building's other residents are aware something happened in 14C and are watching the hallway in shifts — they are not hostile but they will remember faces

Dela Okonkwo has not explained who died in the apartment or why, and the payment being every liquid fund she has suggests the drive contains something that could substantially change her situation in either direction
description:
Dela Okonkwo posted through a single broker vouch with no operational history in the Signal Network. The posting is personal — the language doesn't read like someone who's worked with freelancers before. She knows where the drive is. She knows the window. She's paying everything she has. C-tier jobs at this price point usually mean the client is desperate and the job is simple on paper. Simple on paper is not the same as simple.

The apartment belonged to Dela's brother, Emeka Okonkwo, who died in it three days ago. Arcturus listed the cause as an altercation — a fight that went wrong. Dela doesn't believe it. Emeka worked as an informal data broker out of the Gray Zone 8 — low-level, the Gray Zone-level work, the kind of thing that keeps people fed rather than making anyone rich. The drive behind the ventilation grille was his work archive: client lists, transaction logs, data fragments he'd been paid to hold and pass along. Dela wants it because she believes it contains evidence of what actually happened to her brother — who hired him last, what he was moving. She may be right. She may also be walking a freelancer into lifting evidence from a crime scene that Arcturus is actively investigating because someone with more resources than Emeka Okonkwo wants that drive gone before Arcturus finds it, and Dela is the unwitting instrument of that goal.
story_hooks: The drive is where Dela said it would be, but so is a second drive she didn't know about — identical casing, clearly placed deliberately alongside the first

One of the Arcturus forensic technicians running the sweep on 14C is running it slowly and carefully in a way that suggests they are also looking for something specific that isn't in their official case brief
